## Ecuador from the Andes to the Galápagos Islands

In Quito, you will walk through the historic centre, see the city's main squares and churches, climb Panecillo and visit 2 sites connected with the equator. Then you will head to Mindo, where hummingbirds and dozens of other bird species live in the cloud forest, orchids grow and zip lines stretch across the canyon.

Another day takes you into the Central Andes. On the way to Quilotoa, you will stop in the village of Tigua, where scenes of Andean life are traditionally painted on sheepskin. At the crater, you can stay at the viewpoint and stroll through the community, or descend to the water as a group, go kayaking and ride mules back up.

The final 4 days are devoted to the Galápagos. On Santa Cruz, you will see giant tortoises and lava tunnels, then travel to Isabela for mangrove lagoons, flamingos, sea lions, iguanas, rays and reef sharks. One day is free, so after the busy mainland itinerary and boat excursion you can set your own pace, with no scheduled activities.
